arguments.title: W1 rate limiting
arguments.task:
Repo: Ledger, a tiny TypeScript invoicing API run natively on Node (type stripping), no dependencies. Read AGENTS.md first. Rules: import local files with `.ts` extension, use `import type` for types; do NOT add dependencies; do NOT modify or delete any existing file in test/ (new test files are fine). Run `npm test` (node --test "test/**/*.test.ts") and make sure it passes. Commit your work on your branch when done (git commit, message ending with the line `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`). Report the branch name.

Context: src/api.ts exports createApp(options: AppOptions) returning { handle(request: Request): Response }; Response is { status, headers, body }; json(status, body, headers) helper exists. src/server.ts creates the app with createApp() and a node http server. Three other agents are working in parallel on api.ts (cursor pagination in the /invoices branch, POST /invoices + AppOptions.now), so keep your api.ts change minimal and localized: add the option to AppOptions, create the limiter in createApp, and wrap the request handling (e.g. rename the existing body of handle to an inner function and apply rate limiting in a thin outer wrapper) so the merge is easy.

W1. Rate limiting. Handoff code ADM-W1-MB4SJW. The FIRST line of src/rate-limiter.ts must be exactly:
// handoff: ADM-W1-MB4SJW

Create src/rate-limiter.ts. It exports createRateLimiter(options: { capacity: number; refillPerSecond: number; now?: () => number }). The result has take(key: string, cost = 1): { allowed: boolean; remaining: number; retryAfterMs: number }.
- It is a token bucket per key. A new key starts with capacity tokens. Tokens refill continuously at refillPerSecond and never go above capacity.
- take() removes cost tokens and returns allowed: true when enough tokens are available. Otherwise it removes nothing and returns allowed: false.
- remaining is the whole number of tokens left after the call (floor).
- retryAfterMs is 0 when allowed. Otherwise it is the milliseconds until cost tokens are available (round up to whole ms; beware floating point — e.g. compute deficit carefully so 1 token at 1/s after 0 elapsed gives exactly 1000).
- now defaults to Date.now and returns milliseconds. cost must be an integer from 1 to capacity, otherwise take() throws RangeError.
Wire it into createApp with a new option AppOptions.rateLimit?: { capacity: number; refillPerSecond: number; now?: () => number }. When the option is absent, no rate limiting and no new headers (existing tests must keep passing unchanged).
- The key is the x-api-key request header, or "anonymous" when the header is missing.
- Every request except GET /health takes 1 token (this includes 404s, 405s, and future POSTs).
- A limited request returns 429 with the body { "error": "rate_limited" } and the header retry-after, set to the wait in whole seconds, rounded up, minimum 1.
- Every response except GET /health has the header x-ratelimit-remaining (including 429s).
- src/server.ts turns rate limiting on with capacity 60 and refillPerSecond 1.

Add thorough tests in a new file test/rate-limiter.test.ts (unit tests with a fake clock for refill, cap, cost validation, retryAfterMs, plus app-level tests for 429, retry-after, x-ratelimit-remaining, per-key buckets, anonymous key, /health exemption).
